content.comment_body: Is it possible to connect two [product_name] operator displays to a single [product_name] controller? I am using a [product_name] controller to manage a production line operating in two separate areas, and I want to provide displays so that operators in both locations can see which machine has stopped. Any advice would be appreciated.

As mentioned earlier, connecting two operator displays to one [product_name] isn't possible. However, you could use the onboard [product_name] display in one area so the operator can view it, while placing the operator display in another area of your machine. It's possible to program both the [product_name] display and the operator display to show the same information, or customize messages so some are shown only on one display or the other.
It's possible to use the front panel of the installation door to mount the [product_name] display. The maximum installation width is eight modules, each 17.8 mm wide.

I've occasionally tested parallel operation myself. One approach is to use a two-way circuit that separates the signal line and supply voltage, switching them via changeover contacts. We have found limited success with this method. Both operator displays cannot be used simultaneously, but by switching locations, you could make it work in alternating mode. With newer models, the Ethernet connection allows additional display options alongside the operator display.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are discussing how to connect two operator displays to a single [product_name] controller to improve visibility across separate production zones. Officially, only one operator display can be directly connected, limiting simultaneous viewing for multiple operators. Users have suggested partial workarounds such as using the onboard display or implementing a manual switching circuit, but these solutions do not allow concurrent operation across both areas.
